title: In My Family App, Every Agent Borrows One Person's Permissions
description: When I built Kin, a small private app for my household's people, dates and providers, the most important design rule was that an agent never gets its own access, only a slice of the person who owns it.

title: My Agent Can Draft Posts. It Cannot Publish Them.
description: Why I stopped letting an agent drive a browser to post on X and built a small scheduler where agent tokens can only propose drafts and the software enforces my approval.

title: Agile Was Built for Expensive Code
description: When agents write most of the code, the hard part of agile shifts to intent, context, guardrails and verification. Here's what I think changes and what stays.

title: I Built My X Dashboard as One Binary, and the Agent Kept It That Way
description: How I built xstats, a small self-hosted X stats dashboard, with Grok Bot's help, and why keeping it to one Go binary and one SQLite file made the agent a better collaborator.

title: Boring Agents Win
description: The agents that ship in production are the ones nobody wants to demo.

title: Hello World
description: Kicking off the blog with a quick hello.
